title: Edge proxy request ordering bug causing cascading 5xx & retry amplification
creator: Ava Chen
description: High-severity customer escalations observed between 2025-02-16 and 2025-02-18: multiple tenants reported transient 5xx spikes and timeouts coincident with heavy client-side retries. Initial investigation points to an ordering bug in the edge proxy that allows duplicate forwarded requests to reach the runtime out-of-order, interacting poorly with KV cache eviction TTLs and per-backend connection pools. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, hotfix, staged rollout, and postmortem items.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a tenant burst by sending 200 concurrent requests with identical prompt prefixes and X-Request-ID reused across retries.
2) Configure client-side retry policy to aggressive retry (3 retries, no jitter) to mimic escalated customer SDK settings.
3) Observe edge-proxy logs: multiple forwarded requests for same X-Request-ID occasionally reordered when routed across proxy worker threads.
4) Observe runtime: KV cache entries evicted early due to TTL churn and connection pool exhaustion, leading to 502/504 responses under load.
root_cause: Race in edge proxy worker handoff: when a retried request arrives shortly after the original, the proxy sometimes routes it to a different worker which forwards it before the original's cancellation/fallback path completes. This produced duplicate in-flight requests that bypassed idempotency/dedup protections. Combined with a recently tightened kvcache TTL compaction job, this caused rapid cache churn and transient backend failures under concurrent bursts.
mitigation: Short-term (hotfix): patch edge proxy to honor X-Request-ID dedup table for 250ms window before forwarding duplicate requests; deploy to gateway-canary and gateway-1 region.
Operational: add temporary per-tenant in-flight cap at ingress (default 50 -> emergency 10 for affected tenants) and enable request shaping for high-rate tenants.
Runtime config: back off the kvcache aggressive compaction window from 60s to 180s to avoid eviction storms during bursts until durable kernel scheduler fixes land.
Customer comms: notify impacted tenants of mitigation and estimated timeline; provide opt-out for immediate per-tenant cap removal if they accept reduced reliability risk.
resolution_plan: 1) Merge edge proxy dedupe patch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/762) with unit + integration tests that simulate worker handoff races.
2) Add deterministic ordering handshake between proxy workers to ensure cancellation messages are applied before duplicate forwards.
3) Add an observability metric 'proxy.duplicate_forward_rate' and a traced span to link request lineage through the proxy -> runtime path.
4) Revisit kvcache compaction heuristic: introduce burst-aware compaction that keeps 'hot' prefixes until low-traffic steady state is detected.
rollout_plan: Canary1 (gateway-canary): 10% of traffic for 2 hours, smoke tests for duplicate_forward_rate and 502/504 rates.
Canary2 (gateway-us-west): 30% for 4 hours, monitor latency P95, kvcache hit rate, and connection pool saturation.
Gradual rollout to remaining regions over 48 hours if metrics stable; immediate rollback if 5xx rate increases by >10% relative to baseline.
During rollout, keep per-tenant emergency cap enabled for top-20 impacted tenants for 72 hours.
verification: Pre-merge: unit tests for dedupe table, integration test simulating worker reorder (CI: edge-proxy/integration/reorder_spec).
Post-deploy: observe proxy.duplicate_forward_rate -> target <0.1% and hosted-api 5xx rate -> return to baseline within 1 hour.
Customer validation: reach out to the three reported customers (AcmePayments, MonoChat, ScholasticaAI) for acceptance testing and confirm no further escalations.
